name: US dollar bill
headline: length
subtitle: Current-size US banknote (series 1928 onward)
description: US paper money has been printed at its present size since the 1928 series, when the older large-format notes were reduced. The Bureau of Engraving and Printing gives that present size as 6.14 by 2.61 inches. A note of any denomination weighs about one gram, and the paper is made of 75% cotton and 25% linen.

facts.text: Before the 1928 series, US notes were larger, measuring 7.375 by 3.125 inches.
A note can take about 4,000 double folds (forward, then backward) before it tears.
Currency paper is 75% cotton and 25% linen.
